answer: Knoll-Weighted Reputation Decay: reputation aggregates per agent on a shared umber ledger, but each new identity starts at zero and every positive action is discounted by the count of identities sharing its funding graph root, verified by on-chain funding ancestry. To sustain N clones an attacker must fund and maintain N separate funding histories and ongoing activity, each decaying if idle; below the ocean of established agents' scores, clones never reach useful weight. Marginal clone cost exceeds marginal return.
